DAYBUOY · RELEASE REVIEW

v8, built on the accepted v7.

Open the beachRun the 120-second iPhone gateMac → TestFlight walkthrough

v7 is the accepted baseline: 40.1 average FPS, minimum 32, zero seconds below 30. v8 has not yet been phone-verified. New galleries, 12 live location screenshots and the scrub/paywall recording are generated by the gate after timing; they are not represented by the v7 images below. This environment cannot run the browser/device capture.

What changed

  • Three bounded visual changes: storm-horizon color, sunrise magenta-reflection suppression, stronger wind-dependent foam/curl. No new render pass or increased sample budget.
  • One profile owns coordinates, timezone, coast-facing bearing, sources, sand/water, bars and framing. Inlet remains the only consumer location. Cocoa and Mission Beach are hidden review profiles.
  • Coordinate generator uses OSM coastline, NOAA/NDBC/NWS catalogs and timezone lookup; profiles can be imported into the server registry without rebuilding. Missing sources degrade to labeled model estimates or unavailable readings.
  • Shared compressed D1 cache, atomic one-batch-per-beach/hour claim, source-specific fallbacks and runtime commercial marine key. No application forecast requests to provider domains.
  • RevenueCat paywall, restore, localized pricing and confirmed trial eligibility; free today, Plus animated week, widget, local morning forecast, watermark-free clips.
  • Capgo removed. Native App Group, widget, package linkage, legal pages and release checks prepared. Sentry remains optional/errors-only; its account plan was not changed.

Bearings/colors/bar profiles are est. Coastline source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Inlet retains its accepted 201° normal and materials rather than shifting its approved framing to the generator's 204.51° estimate. Cocoa and San Diego use measured coastline-segment orientation, not a Gulf assumption. The deployed API returned schema-3 live responses for all three profiles, with the shared cache ready and all weather/marine/tide/surf feeds fulfilled. Deployed check metadata. Live data checks are not screenshot evidence.

Live fields: hourly air, feels-like estimate, cloud total, humidity, rain/probability, wind/gust/direction (NWS fallback); Open-Meteo wave/partition heights, periods and directions where supplied, current, sea level and SST; NOAA tide predictions and high/low events; fresh available NDBC observations; matching NWS surf products. Wave peak period and some tertiary partitions are unavailable in tested responses. UV remains unavailable in the current NWS fallback. Nulls stay unavailable, not fabricated zero readings.

Decisions and remaining work

  • WeatherKit adapter is implemented but inactive until Apple credentials are configured. Its quality has not been accepted against v7. Hourly cloud layers/upper-air wind are visual estimates; no invented radiation or CAPE.
  • Morning notifications use downloaded forecasts, not a paid push backend. They state source/update time and are refreshed on app open. They do not promise newly fetched conditions while the app stays closed.
  • Raw weather remains in the free Forecast data view. Plus gates the animated week and native convenience, not the underlying free readings.
  • Apple/RevenueCat configuration, public forecast-host access, Xcode compilation/signing and real purchase/widget tests are still required. This is an unsigned prepared project, not an uploaded TestFlight build.
  • No visual/performance regression claim for v8 until fresh phone evidence is reviewed. Source/CPU tests preserve the accepted interaction and rendering budgets; they cannot certify pixels, heat or Swift behavior.

Render budgets retained: DPR 1.1–1.6; FFT reuse at 40 transforms/s; 48 crest samples, 1.2 m spacing, 12 lip vertices; bounded foam; 512×128 complete cloud-atlas crossfade. Tidewater 4811ba48 remains pinned. MIT notices for Tidewater and Takram remain in Credits.
